regions.full_page: after-noon by a Catholic neighbor. .... "Ill do anything to please the good God if he'll only spare my poor, dear husband"., she answered. "Then, Mrs. W.", answered, "This is about what I would advise you. "Make a promise or proposition to Almighty God in your ovm honest way as a methodist, that if your husband gives the doc- tors a surprise tomorrow or by the end of the week (it was Tuesday), you'll be earnest in looking into the difference or rather the re- lationship between your denomination and the "Mother Church". They returned the following Friday with Mr. W. all taped-up but smiling. He had come home from the Univ .- hospital in Ann Arbor next day Wed. Doctors Wood and Pete had pronounced his recovery miraculous. . . October 18th a year and a half later they came back - the last time I saw them and he looked and acted as he'd never been sick. This, however, was two nights after she had phoned me, lament- ing that he was not well, etc, and I had admonished her to do some- thing toward the fulfilling of the promese she had made so many months before, if her husband were spared her. Besides, I had given her a copy of the "Mystical City of God", - the winderful Life of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which I honestly consider her own autobiography; the actual writer being as her secretary Venerable Mother Mary of Jesus, of Agrada Spain. He especially seemed enthused over the book that night - had evid- been on the "job" of reading the book, those couple of days.
